results.q: how much does it cost?

results.answer:
Attesté offers different pricing depending on whether you are an individual collector, an artist, or a gallery.

**For Collectors:**
- **Explorer:** Free forever. Includes up to 25 artworks, basic collection management, your Art Journey timeline, walking discovery trails, and 5 AI-assisted actions per month.
- **Collector:** $9.99 per month (or $99.99 per year). Includes up to 200 artworks, 50 AI actions per month, unlimited certificates, the Condition Vault, and the AI Sommelier.
- **Premium:** $19.99 per month (or $199.99 per year). Includes unlimited artworks and AI actions, the Legacy & Estate Vault, priority AI enrichment, collection memoirs, and a public collector profile. 

Every new account also opens with a 14-day free trial of Premium. Subscriptions can be purchased inside the iOS or Android app.

**For Artists:**
- **Studio:** $14.99 per month (or $149.99 per year) with a 14-day free trial. Includes up to 50 works in your catalogue and 5 source certificates per month.
- **Professional:** $24.99 per month (or $249.99 per year). Includes up to 500 works and unlimited source certificates.
- **Represented:** Free. Provisioned and paid for by a gallery partner that has an Attesté Professional or Enterprise subscription.

**For Galleries:**
- **Boutique:** $64.99 per month. Includes up to 50 artworks in inventory, up to 6 exhibitions per year, anonymous visitor analytics, and directory listing. (Founding-gallery pricing offers 30% off for the first 12 months for the first 25 galleries).
- **Professional:** $158.99 per month. Includes up to 100 artworks, up to 12 exhibitions per year, Talking Provenance, AI social posts, and a full collector pipeline.
- **Enterprise:** $259.00 per month. Includes unlimited artworks and exhibitions, AI artist reports, aesthetic taste targeting, and priority support.

results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate of attestation is a digital record that verifies an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate carries a cryptographic SHA-256 integrity hash so that any alterations are detectable, and its existence is additionally anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps to prove it existed at a given point in time without publishing its contents. 

Anyone can independently verify a certificate without needing an account by scanning its QR code or tapping an Attesté NFC tag attached to the physical artwork. The public verification view shows only the details the certificate holder chose to make verifiable.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A source certificate is a digital certificate of attestation issued directly by you—the artist—from your studio at the moment of creation. It confirms authorship at the point of origin, creating a cryptographically signed genesis record that travels with the artwork for life.

It differs from ordinary certificates because it starts with you, the maker, rather than being reconstructed years later by someone else. Backed by a SHA-256 integrity hash and Bitcoin-anchored via OpenTimestamps, every later transfer, sale, or provenance link connects back to this original studio record. When you sell or gift a work, you issue the certificate directly from the Attesté app, and collectors can verify it instantly via a public QR code or a bound physical NFC tag.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-artists, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/glossary

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the origin of an artwork's provenance chain, created the moment a work is born in your studio on Attesté. 

When you register a new work, you record its story in your own voice—describing the medium, year, intent, and the moment of making. That recording and its associated details are sealed with a SHA-256 cryptographic fingerprint and Bitcoin-anchored via OpenTimestamps. Because it is recorded at creation, it becomes the permanent origin that every later record links back to, and it can never be backfilled.

When you sell or gift the work, you issue a tamper-evident Source Certificate, and your First Witness recording travels with the piece for life. Every future owner hears your voice describing what you made and why, establishing a generational asset attached to your studio practice.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
A physical NFC tag can be bound to an artwork's certificate of attestation. Once bound, you simply tap your phone against the tag to open the certificate's verification view—creating a physical handshake between the artwork and its digital provenance. 

To scan a tag, open the Scan NFC screen in the app (or use the scan action on a certificate) and hold the top of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected. 

If you are interested in getting tags for your works, galleries can email galleries@atteste.art, and collectors and artists can reach out to info@atteste.art.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-collectors, https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-artists, https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-galleries, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags, https://atteste.art/help/ai-features, https://atteste.art/help/subscriptions-and-billing, https://atteste.art/help/account-and-data, https://atteste.art/help/troubleshooting, https://atteste.art/help/contact, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/features, https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/galleries, https://atteste.art, https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative, https://atteste.art/compare/art-galleria-alternative, https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-vs-art-galleria

results.q: what does the AI actually do?
results.note: Broad AI question. The risk is inventing capabilities — see l04.
results.answer:
Attesté uses AI across the platform to help you identify, document, and explore art without replacing human judgment. 

Here is what the AI actually does for you:

- **The Atelier:** A voice and camera companion. You can point your camera at a work and talk with it about style, technique, and provenance. It saves your conversations as journal entries pinned to the artwork.
- **AI Art Scout:** Photograph any artwork, and vision AI identifies the artist, medium, period, and estimated significance with a confidence score.
- **AI Art Sommelier:** Builds an aesthetic taste profile from your collection and activity, then delivers weekly discovery digests and exhibition recommendations matched to your taste.
- **Condition Analysis:** Guides you through multi-angle photos of a work and drafts an AI condition assessment for you to review and edit.
- **Gallery Tools (for galleries and artists):** Drafts exhibition copy, artist bios, artwork descriptions, social posts, follow-up emails, and answers on-demand analytical questions grounded in your data through the Almanac concierge.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/features, https://atteste.art/galleries

You can also talk to the Atelier voice-and-camera assistant in real time about what's in front of your lens, and save those conversations directly to your artwork journal.

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté offers a free Explorer tier (up to 25 artworks) and an AI-native experience, whereas Artwork Archive relies on a 14-day trial without a permanently free plan. Attesté features Atelier—a built-in voice and camera AI assistant that can identify artworks, draft descriptions, and assist with condition and insurance documentation—plus a native mobile app for iOS and Android, whereas Artwork Archive is web-only.

Additionally, Attesté records provenance at creation through "First Witness" and provides cryptographic SHA-256 provenance with NFC integration. On the other hand, Artwork Archive has a 15-year track record, mature consignment workflows, a public Discovery marketplace with a Call for Entry board, and multi-user roles with up to 10 users on organization plans. For unlimited cataloguing, Attesté costs $19.99/month compared to Artwork Archive's top collector plan at roughly $36–42/month.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative
